questions.text: Why can a causal decoder reuse an earlier token’s cached keys and values after a new token is appended, with fixed weights and deterministic inference?

options.A: Every token in the growing sequence has identical keys and values.
options.B: Its causal hidden states cannot depend on tokens appended later.
options.C: Appending a token freezes the next-token probability distribution.
options.D: The cache replaces every earlier token with the newest token.

questions.explanation: Causal attention prevents an earlier position from depending on later positions, so appending a token does not invalidate earlier per-layer keys and values.
